title: Metals, non-metals and metalloids
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers only metals and non-metals and is written for Year 10, while this point also teaches metalloids and must suit Stage 4, so it is broader than the bank card and needs a new point.

draft.title: Metals, non-metals and metalloids
card: Metals are shiny, conduct heat and electricity, and can be bent or hammered without breaking. Copper and iron are metals.
Most non-metals are dull and do not conduct heat or electricity well. Solid ones tend to break when hit. Sulfur and oxygen are non-metals.
Metalloids have some properties of each group. Silicon is shiny like a metal, but it conducts electricity only a little and it is brittle.
The properties of a material decide how it is used. Copper is used in wires because it conducts electricity and bends easily.
draft.remember: Metals conduct and bend, most non-metals do not, and metalloids sit in between.

a.q: A solid element is dull, snaps when hit with a hammer and does not conduct electricity. What is it most likely to be?
a.why: Dull, brittle and not conducting are properties of most non-metals. A metal would be shiny and would bend, and a metalloid would conduct a little.
a.clue: Think about which group does not conduct.

b.q: Priya needs a material for the handle of a cooking pot. It must not carry heat to her hand. Which property should she look for?
b.why: A handle should stop heat reaching the hand, so the material must conduct heat poorly. Metals conduct heat well, which is why they suit the pot itself but not the handle.
b.clue: The handle should do the opposite of the pot.
